RT_E_RATCHET_METRIC_UNAVAILABLE.why: The W356 lane could not mint it (it owned no `src/**` file) and no lane owned `src/lib/errors.ts` in W357 either, so W357 armed the debt here. The residual is honest and recorded: the ratchet still CLASSIFIES its unavailable readings by CAUSE through the three long-standing codes (`RT_E_RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` missing input, `RT_E_PROJECT_MISSING` artifact absent, `RT_E_VALIDATION` reader shape changed), so this code has no emitter site YET — adopting it for the "producer ran, no usable reading" site is a follow-up that changes which causes hard-fail, and is the boundary owner's call, not a silent edit here.

policy.floors: A floor MAY ONLY RISE. Breaching it downward (atLeast) or upward (atMost) is a HARD failure. `reading` is the value measured when the floor was pinned — evidence, never the bar; only `floor` is compared.
policy.unavailable: A metric whose producer cannot be produced reports `unavailable` with a coded reason drawn from EXISTING ERROR_CODE_DOC entries (no code is minted by this lane — see the log's follow-up note). Two causes are distinguished, because they are different facts: a MISSING INPUT (`RT_E_RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` — the producer was not run in this invocation, e.g. no --gate was passed) is reported loudly but does NOT fail; a BROKEN OR ABSENT PRODUCER (`RT_E_PROJECT_MISSING` artifact absent, `RT_E_VALIDATION` reader shape changed) on a `status:"enforced"` metric is a HARD failure (fail closed). An unavailable reading NEVER reads as a pass.
policy.pendingFirstGreen: `status:"pending-first-green"` means the floor already names the HONEST bar (usually 0) but the tree is red today, so the floor is REPORTED and not enforced. It must never be lowered; the boundary owner flips it to `enforced` on the first green tree.
policy.readingPinned: A floor equal to the current reading (`readingPinned: true`) is not a target and not a weakening: it locks in today's reading so any future rise is permanent.
policy.uncovered: A kind with no emitted corpus case reports `uncovered` (floor null) and NEVER `pass`.
policy.cost: `estimatedCostUsd` stays null everywhere: no spend is ever fabricated.
